answer:
基于本数据（requirements_engineering_for_ML-enabled_systems.csv，276 行；剔除 82 名 Suspended 未作答者后有效样本 n=194），Q10 文档格式栏位为二元 quoted/not quoted 编码，'quoted' 计为采用该格式。在十种具体文档格式中（排除 Not Documented、Others/Others_Free 等 catch-all），按使用比例点估计排序，使用最少的两种文档格式为：

1) BDD Scenarios —— 4/194 = 2.06%（bootstrap 95% CI [0.515, 4.124]），最少；
2) ML Canvas —— 15/194 = 7.73%（bootstrap 95% CI [4.124, 11.856]），次少。

其后依次为 Vision Document / Goal Models（14.95%）、Data Models（17.5%）、Use Case Models（19.6%）、Prototypes（21.6%）、Requirements Lists（26.3%）、User Stories（32.5%）、Notebooks（34.0%）。

补充说明（区分样本结论与原研究数字）：题目所引 10.13%（95% CI [9.926, 10.333]）与 4.366%（95% CI [4.231, 4.501]）系原研究（由 CI 宽度反推样本量约 8.4 万–8.8 万）的统计量，本 276 行样本经 bootstrap 无法逐位重现（本样本点估计为 2.06%/7.73%，CI 亦宽 10–20 倍）；但排名方向一致——最少为 BDD Scenarios、次少为 ML Canvas，与题目数字（4.366% 对应最少者、10.13% 对应次少者）相符。故数据支撑的结论为：最少使用的两种文档格式是 BDD Scenarios 与 ML Canvas。

payload.hypothesis: Among the ten concrete documentation formats surveyed for requirements in ML-enabled system projects, BDD Scenarios are the least used (4/194 = 2.06%, 95% bootstrap CI [0.515, 4.124]) and ML Canvas is the second-least used (15/194 = 7.73%, 95% CI [4.124, 11.856]); the question's 10.13%/4.366% figures are original-study estimates (implied sample ~85k) that this 276-row sample cannot reproduce exactly, but the ranking direction is consistent (BDD Scenarios least, ML Canvas second-least).
payload.workflow: Loaded 276-row CSV (ID unique => one row per respondent). Q10_ML_Documentation_* recoded as binary 'quoted'/'not quoted'; '-77' identified as the 82 'Suspended (22)' non-respondents (identical set across all 12 Q10 columns) and excluded => effective n=194. Usage proportion per format = #quoted / 194 over the 10 concrete formats (excluded catch-alls Not Documented, Others, Others_Free). 95% CI via bootstrap percentile (B=10,000, alpha=0.05, seed=42). Ranked by point estimate; BDD Scenarios (2.06%) and ML Canvas (7.73%) are the two least-used. The cited 10.13% [9.926,10.333] and 4.366% [4.231,4.501] imply n~84,452 and 88,012 respectively and are NOT reproducible from this dataset via standard binomial bootstrap; they are attributed to the original larger study, with consistent ranking.
